text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Panel composition alone proves very little. All-women panels appoint men routinely, and a four-person panel in a news division is a plausible random draw. On its own it's not evidence — and raising it will likely be read as sour grapes, damaging you internally where you presumably still work.

The substantive point is different: "strong experience of digital media" against your fifteen years is a real selection criterion, and a legitimate one for a modern newsroom. Seniority isn't automatically the deciding factor.

Your genuine grievance is the unanswered request. Chase that in writing, cite the published criteria, and ask how each was scored. If the reasoning turns out incoherent or post-hoc, reassess then.
